key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks can learn and evolve a puncture-form black-hole spacetime in spherical symmetry while respecting Einstein-equation physics and moving-puncture gauge structure.
engineering_relevance: This offers a compact, differentiable surrogate for numerical relativity data that could accelerate interpolation, continuation, and reconstruction of black-hole simulations.
method: Represent lapse, shift, and regular Z4c variables (chi and gamma_tilde_rr) with a PINN.
Train with a composite loss combining data mismatch, Ricci-tensor residuals, and moving-puncture gauge conditions.
Use limited data to interpolate, extrapolate time evolution, or infer the interior spacetime from exterior observations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful interpolation of NR data, forward evolution from early-time and outer-boundary data, and interior reconstruction from exterior-only data, verified via a learned transformation to Kerr-Schild coordinates.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated in 1+1D spherical symmetry for a single non-spinning black hole, so generalization to full 3D, more dynamic systems, and harder gauge settings remains an implementation challenge.
paper_title: Puncture Evolution with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
